newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-MORE CHAOS AS FLUMINENSE STADIUM RE-OPENED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MORE CHAOS AS FLUMINENSE STADIUM RE-OPENED.

text.p: Fighting between players and coaches from Brazilian clubs Fluminense and America held up play for 10 minutes during a Rio de Janeiro championship match on Wednesday night.
The game was the first to be played at Fluminense's stadium since an incident last year when an oppostion goalkeeper was beaten up by fans and needed an operation to remove a blood clot on his brain.

Trouble started two minutes from the end of Wednesday's match with a clash between America coach Luisinho, who had already been sent off and Fluminense full-back Paulo Roberto. Fighting quickly spread.
Players and officials spent several minutes exchanging punches and kicks. Paulo Roberto was shown the red card along with Mauricio and Rogerio of America. The game ended 1-1.

Fluminense were banned from playing at their stadium after Atletico Paranaense goalkeeper Ricardo Pinto was attacked by fans who invaded the pitch at the end of his team's 3-2 win in a Brazilian championship match in November.
He later needed an operation after becoming partly paralised and was sidelined for nearly two months.

The Rio de Janeiro championship suffered a serious blow to its credibility earlier this year when Fluminense, Flamengo and Botafogo boycotted the opening day because they did not like the rules of the competition.
A compromise was eventually reached with the Rio de Janeiro federation, which brought in a new format, and the rebel clubs are now playing their way through a backlog of fixtures.
